1.w: A Psalm of Asaph. Surely God [is] good to Israel, to those pure of heart.

2.w: And [as for] me, at a little stretching out of my feet, my steps had nearly poured out.

3.w: For I was envious of those boasting [when] I saw the prosperity of the wicked.

4.w: For there are no pangs until their death, and their body [is] fat.

5.w: They [are] not in the trouble of mankind, and with men they are not are they plagued.

6.w: Therefore pride is their necklace; a garment of violence is a covering for them.

7.w: Their eye has bulged out from fat, the imaginations of their heart overflow.

8.w: They scoff and speak with malice; from a high place they speak oppression.

9.w: They have set their mouth in the heavens, and their tongue walks through the earth.

10.w: Therefore his people turn here, and waters of fullness are wrung out for them.

11.w: And they say, “How can God know? And is there knowledge in the Most High?”

12.w: Behold, these [are] the wicked, and at ease always, they have increased in wealth.

13.w: Surely [in] vain I have cleansed my heart, and I have washed my hands in innocence.

14.w: For I have been stricken all the day, and chastened in the morning.

15.w: If I had said, “I will speak like this,” behold, I would have betrayed the generation of Your sons.

16.w: And I thought to know this—it [was] toil in my eyes—

17.w: until I came to the sanctuary of God, [and] discerned their end.

18.w: Surely You set them on slick ground; You make them fall to destruction.

19.w: How they have become a desolation in a moment! They are swept away completely by terrors.

20.w: As a dream from awakening, O Lord, in rousing Yourself, You shall despise their image.

21.w: For my heart had grown sour, and my kidneys pierce themselves.

22.w: And I [was] brutish and could not know; I was a beast before You.

23.w: And I [am] always with You; You hold my right hand.

24.w: May You lead me with Your counsel, and afterward You will receive me [in] glory!

25.w: Who [is] unto me in the heavens? And besides You I do not take delight on the earth.

26.w: My flesh and my heart may be consumed, the rock of my heart and my portion [is] God to the age.

27.w: For behold, those far from You will perish. You destroy everyone prostituting himself from You!

28.w: But I—the nearness of God [is] good for me—I have placed my refuge in the Lord YHWH, to recount all Your works.
